paper.title: May 2024 Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL Paper 1 TZ2
paper.solution_status: Independent worked solutions — checked against the official IB markscheme

questions.accessible_text:
1. [Maximum mark: 5]

The graph of y=f(x), 0≤x≤10, intercepts the axes at (10,0) and (0,5).

[Diagram: grid 0≤x,y≤10. A decreasing concave-up curve from (0,5) to (10,0), through approximately (1,3), (2,2), (4,1), and (9,0).]

(a) Write down (i) f(4); (ii) (f∘f)(4); (iii) f⁻¹(3). [3]

(b) Sketch y=f⁻¹(x), clearly showing its axis intercepts. [2]
questions.solution: (a) f(4)=1, f(f(4))=f(1)=3, and f⁻¹(3)=1. (b) Reflect in y=x: the inverse intercepts are (0,10) and (5,0), and it passes through (2,2), (1,4), and (3,1).

questions.accessible_text:
3. [Maximum mark: 5]

(a) Solve 3m²+5m−2=0. [3]

(b) Hence or otherwise, solve 3×9ˣ+5×3ˣ−2=0. [2]
questions.summary: Use a quadratic substitution in an exponential equation.
questions.solution: (a) (3m−1)(m+2)=0, so m=1/3 or −2. (b) With m=3ˣ>0, only 3ˣ=1/3 is valid, giving x=−1.

questions.accessible_text:
4. [Maximum mark: 7]

[Diagram: quadrilateral OABC on axes; O is the origin, A lies on the positive x-axis, B is directly above A, C is upper-left of B, and dashed OB is the symmetry axis.]

OABC is symmetrical about [OB]. A=(6,0), C=(3,3√3).

(a) (i) Write down the midpoint of [AC]. (ii) Hence or otherwise, find the equation of the line through O and B. [4]

(b) Given [OA] is perpendicular to [AB], find the area of OABC. [3]
questions.solution: (a)(i) (9/2,3√3/2). (ii) Its gradient from O is √3/3, so OB: y=(√3/3)x. (b) At x=6, B has y=2√3. Triangle OAB has area 6√3; symmetry gives area OABC=12√3.

questions.accessible_text:
5. [Maximum mark: 6]

A bird nests in Spring with probability k and in Summer with probability k/2.

[Tree: Spring nesting k and not nesting blank; following either outcome, Summer nesting k/2 and not nesting blank.]

(a) Complete the not-nesting probabilities in terms of k. [2]

P(not nesting in Spring and not nesting in Summer)=5/9.

(b) (i) Show 9k²−27k+8=0. (ii) Both k=1/3 and k=8/3 satisfy it. State why only k=1/3 is valid. [4]
questions.summary: Complete a probability tree and solve its quadratic.
questions.solution: (a) Spring not nesting: 1−k; Summer not nesting: 1−k/2 on both branches. (b) (1−k)(1−k/2)=5/9 gives 9k²−27k+8=0. Since probabilities cannot exceed 1, k=8/3 is invalid; k=1/3 is valid.

questions.accessible_text:
6. [Maximum mark: 8]

f(x)=2(x+3)/[3(x+2)], x∈ℝ, x≠−2.

[Graph: rational curve on −6≤x,y≤6, with vertical asymptote x=−2 and dashed horizontal asymptote; intercepts (−3,0) and (0,1).]

(a) Write down the horizontal asymptote. [1]

Let g(x)=mx+1, m∈ℝ, m≠0.

(b) (i) Write down the number of solutions to f(x)=g(x) for m>0. (ii) Determine m for exactly one solution. (iii) Determine the range of m for two solutions with x≥0. [7]
questions.summary: Analyze intersections with a line family.
questions.solution: (a) y=2/3. Equating gives 3mx²+(6m+1)x=0, so x=0 or x=−(6m+1)/(3m). (b)(i) 2. (ii) Coincidence at m=−1/6. (iii) Requiring the second root positive gives −1/6<m<0.

questions.accessible_text:
7. [Maximum mark: 12]

Alex swims only when water is at least 15°C. He models midday temperature by f(x)=a sin(bx)+c, 0≤x≤12, x months after 1 May, a,b,c>0.

[Graph: sinusoid starting at 15°C, maximum 20°C at x=3, minimum 10°C at x=9, returning to 15°C at x=12.]

(a) Show b=π/6. [1]

(b) Write down (i) a; (ii) c. [2]

At a holiday destination g(x)=3.5sin(πx/6)+11.

(c) (i) Find the temperature on 1 October (x=5). (ii) Show it is never warm enough for Alex to swim. [6]

(d) Given g(x)=0.7f(x)+q, determine q. [3]

8. [Maximum mark: 17]

f′(x)=(2x+2)/(x²+2x+2), x∈ℝ.

(a) (i) Show x²+2x+2>0 for all x. (ii) Hence find where f is increasing. [3]

(b) (i) Write down x where f′(x)=0. (ii) Show f″(x)=(−2x²−4x)/(x²+2x+2)². (iii) Hence justify this x gives a local minimum. [7]

Given f(2)=3+ln10,

(c) find f(x). [4]

(d) Find the normal at (2,3+ln10). [3]
questions.summary: Analyze, integrate, and find a normal from a derivative.
questions.solution: (a) Denominator=(x+1)²+1>0; f increases for x>−1. (b) x=−1. Quotient rule gives the stated f″, and f″(−1)=2>0, so it is a local minimum. (c) f=ln(x²+2x+2)+C; the condition gives C=3. (d) f′(2)=3/5, so y−(3+ln10)=−(5/3)(x−2).

questions.accessible_text:
9. [Maximum mark: 16]

Arithmetic sequence a,p,q,… has nonzero terms.

(a) Show 2p−q=a. [2]

Geometric sequence a,s,t,… has nonzero terms.

(b) Show s²=at. [2]

Both start with a and q=t=1.

(c) Show p>1/2. [2]

For a=9, s>0, q=t=1:

(d) Write the first four terms of (i) the arithmetic sequence; (ii) the geometric sequence. [4]

They form a new arithmetic sequence uₙ with u₁=9+ln9, u₂=5+ln3, u₃=1+ln1.

(e) (i) Find its common difference in terms of ln3. (ii) Show Σᵢ₌₁¹⁰uᵢ=−90−25ln3. [6]
questions.summary: Relate and combine arithmetic and geometric sequences.
questions.solution: (a) p−a=q−p gives 2p−q=a. (b) s/a=t/s gives s²=at. (c) a=2p−1=s²>0, hence p>1/2. (d) Arithmetic: 9,5,1,−3; geometric: 9,3,1,1/3. (e) d=−4−ln3. Then S₁₀=5[2(9+2ln3)+9(−4−ln3)]=−90−25ln3.
